subjects.name: Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war

summary: Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman rose from a minor royal branch to rule Saudi Arabia from 2015, waging a devastating war in Yemen, purging rivals and dissidents, torturing activists and ordering the 2018 murder of Jamal Khashoggi.

evidence.note: 1744-45 alliance of Muhammad ibn Saud and al-Wahhab founds the first Saudi state
as defense minister he orders the March 2015 intervention in Yemen
June 2017 palace confrontation forces crown prince MBN to resign
Khashoggi killed and dismembered at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul
MBN studies in Portland and trains with the FBI; ties to US security agencies
1979 seizure of the Grand Mosque in Mecca and the clerical backlash after it
al-Qaeda declares war on the kingdom; MBN leads the counterterror campaign
blockade and strikes on farms used starvation as a weapon; genocide framing
MBS curbs the religious police after decades of clerical power
real estate ventures and business deals that built his early fortune
detailed account of waterboarding, shocks and beatings of women activists

notes: covered_span starts at the 1744 Saud-Wahhab pact: Part 1 spends most of its time on House of Saud history (secondary subject). End is 2026 per the lifetime rule (subject alive). Narrative stops around 2018-2021 with only brief Trump-era and Yemen death-toll remarks, so reaches_present is false. MBN's birth year 1959 is stated; his and MBS's living status taken from the transcript. ottoman-empire polity is for the destruction of the first Saudi state.
